info.title: SockOdds API
info.description: Bookmaker prices SockOdds records itself, readable identifiers, recorded price history and graded results for Australian and global sport.

tags.name: Racing
tags.description: Australian and New Zealand thoroughbred, harness and greyhound racing: meetings and fields, fixed-odds and exchange prices, tote pools and dividends, results, Betfair Starting Price, movement, movers, arbs, form and strike rates.

tags.name: Opportunities
tags.description: Arbitrage, low holds, middles and positive expected value, computed from the prices SockOdds records. Pro and above.

tags.name: Analysis
tags.description: Prices with the bookmaker margin removed, closing prices and closing line value, and line moves across bookmakers. Pro and above.

get.description: Markets and the sides each offers. With `league`, only the markets offered in that league's sport, and only the role sides that sport uses (winner and handicap are home and away in team sports, competitor_1 and competitor_2 in tennis; winner is also offered in UFC).

Find our event from an official event id: ESPN's event id, the AFL's match id (`CD_M` and digits) for AFLW, or the NRL's match id (digits) for the Rugby League World Cup. Send `ref` for one event, or `refs` for up to 100 at once. With `ref`, the response is the event, or 404 when no event carries that id. With `refs`, the response lists the ids that matched, in the order sent, each with its event; ids that match nothing are left out. A merged event returns the event it was merged into. Only official sources can be looked up, never a bookmaker's listing id. Free: costs no credits.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: Who issued the id: `espn`, `afl` for AFLW match ids, or `nrl` for Rugby League World Cup match ids.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: One official event id. Use this or `refs`, not both.

parameters.name: refs
parameters.description: Comma-separated official event ids, at most 100. Use this or `ref`, not both.

get.description: Current prices for one event, grouped by market: each market and outcome appears once, and each outcome lists every bookmaker's price in `prices`, best price first. Markets come in catalogue order, then period, subject and line; outcomes in the market's side order. Use `group_by=bookmaker` for one block per bookmaker instead (the shape v1 launched with). Costs the unique markets returned x regions, in credits. See Plans and limits.

parameters.name: snapshots
parameters.description: Pro and Business only. Adds `opening`, `closing` or both, as requested, to each price, from that bookmaker's own quotes observed strictly before a cutoff (a quote stamped exactly at the cutoff does not count). For every sport but MMA the cutoff is the event's `scheduled_start`, so in-play quotes never count. For an MMA bout, whose `scheduled_start` is its card segment's start, the cutoff once the bout has been observed live or final (first at F) is the last poll that still showed it `scheduled` before F, but never earlier than the earlier of `scheduled_start` and F; a bout never observed live or final uses `scheduled_start`.

get.description: Current prices for a page of events (25 by default, up to 100), grouped by market as on /events/{event_id}/odds unless `group_by=bookmaker`. Pages follow events; a cursor works only with the filters and grouping it was issued for, so follow `links.next`. Filters apply to prices before grouping: an outcome or market with no matching price is left out, and an event with none has an empty `markets` list. Costs credits: featured markets x regions once per page of up to 25 events, other markets per event. See Plans and limits.

Pro and Business only. Upgrade to a WebSocket with your bearer key to receive the current prices for one event, or for up to 20 events in one league, every 15 seconds. Each message is a JSON object whose `type` is `snapshot` (the same body as the matching odds route, grouped by market unless `group_by=bookmaker`), `heartbeat` (nothing changed) or `error` (a problem object, after which the connection closes). A refresh counts towards your allowance like an ordinary odds request only when it sends a new snapshot; a heartbeat (nothing changed) is free. Every refresh still counts towards your per minute request limit. Up to two streams per key. A stream lasts at most one hour; reconnect for a fresh one. The stream is read only; a message from the client closes it. Close codes are 1000 (lifetime reached), 1008 (key, plan or limit change), 1009 (snapshot too large, narrow the filters), 1011 (refresh failed) and 1013 (client reading too slowly).

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: One event. Use this or `league`, not both.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: With `league` only. Events per snapshot, 1 to 20. Defaults to 10.

get.description: Paid plans only. Own observations recorded under the new identities only. No observation predates 22 December 2025 UTC. Changes older than the live store keeps are read from the daily history archive and returned in the same shape and order, so a window reads the same whichever store holds it. Changes are ordered by observation time, then by when they were recorded. A window may not exceed 24 hours. While older history is busy the API answers 503 with a short Retry-After.

Paid plans only. Whole days of history as Parquet files, one file per league and UTC day, from 22 December 2025 up to two days ago. Each file holds the rows /v1/odds/history returns for that league and day, sorted by event and observation time. Own observations only. Listing costs 1 credit.

Paid plans only. Downloads one day of history as a zstd Parquet file. Columns: event_id, market_id, market_key, market_name, period, subject_key, subject_id, subject_name, outcome_id, outcome_name, side, line, bookmaker, observed_at (UTC, milliseconds), kind, decimal_odds, implied_probability. The ETag is the file's SHA-256. At most two downloads at a time per key. Each download costs 100 credits. A file that names a player whose identity came under review after it was built answers 503 until it is rebuilt overnight.

parameters.name: day
parameters.description: UTC day as YYYY-MM-DD.

get.description: Settled outcomes for finished events, graded from official result sources. Each outcome's `verdict` is `won`, `lost`, `void` (stake returned), `dead_heat`, `half_won` or `half_lost`. `half_won` / `half_lost` settle an Asian quarter line (x.25 / x.75) whose two half stakes split: one half won (or lost) at the quoted price and the other half refunded. A dead heat pays `dead_heat_factor` of the stake at the quoted price and loses the rest: a drawn AFL or AFLW head-to-head, a drawn AFLW quarter or half winner, a tied NBL quarter or half winner, and a Rugby League World Cup head-to-head still level after golden point, is a dead heat with a factor of 0.5. Outcomes that official evidence cannot settle are left out, never guessed. Each market settles on its own once official evidence settles all of its outcomes, so a result can be published while other markets on the event are still pending: `settlement` is `partial` and `pending_markets` counts them, and later results for the same event add the newly settled outcomes without changing any verdict already published. Each result also carries `box_score`: the official statistics the result is graded from (score by period, event and team totals, the player statistics SockOdds grades by player ID, and any athletes the source lists that the player registry cannot identify), or null until they have been read.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: Restrict results to one independent event identity.

get.description: Australian and New Zealand races: thoroughbred, harness and greyhound. Paid plans (and the Pro trial); Developer keys get 403. Races come in start order, 25 a page by default, up to 100. With neither starts_after nor starts_before the list runs from 6 hours ago to 48 hours ahead; a window may span at most 8 days. Free: costs no credits. Race ids are SockOdds racing ids such as `thoroughbred_2026-11-17_AUS_scone_r1` (code, date, country, meeting, race number), not the `ev_` ids sport uses.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Comma-separated racing codes: `thoroughbred`, `harness`, `greyhound`.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Comma-separated meeting countries: `AUS`, `NZL`.

parameters.name: starts_after
parameters.description: UTC date and time. Defaults to 6 hours ago.

parameters.name: starts_before
parameters.description: UTC date and time. Defaults to 48 hours after starts_after. At most 8 days after starts_after.

get.description: One race with its field: each runner's number (saddlecloth, or box for greyhounds), name, barrier, jockey (the driver in harness; null for greyhounds), trainer, weight, claim, form figures, silk colours and whether it is scratched or an emergency; and the race's class and conditions, prize money, track condition, weather, rail position and places paid, as stated on the TAB race page (null until that page has been read). `result` carries the placings by runner number and the scratched numbers once the race is resulted, else null; the full result with dividends is at `/racing/races/{race_id}/result`. Free: costs no credits.

Current fixed-odds win and place prices for every runner, one entry per bookmaker, and Betfair Exchange back and lay prices with the size available and the volume matched (AUD). `available` is true while the race has not jumped and the price was observed in the last 600 seconds. Scratched runners carry no prices. Costs 1 credit per region, 5 with opening and closing prices. See Plans and limits.

parameters.name: snapshots
parameters.description: Pro and Business only. Adds `opening` (the first price recorded for the runner, and the bookmaker that offered it) and `closing` (the last price before the jump, and the bookmaker; with the Betfair Exchange back and lay at the jump) per runner, for win and place. `closing` is null until the race has jumped.

get.description: Paid plans only. Every recorded change of a win or place price for one race, by runner and bookmaker, in observation order. A window may span at most 24 hours; racing movement is recorded from 16 November 2026 23:09 UTC. At most `limit` changes are returned; `meta.truncated` is true when the window may hold more, so ask again from the last `observed_at`.

Race meetings: one racing code at one track on one day, each with its races in start order and the track condition, weather and rail position last stated for it. Same plans, filters and window as the races list (6 hours ago to 48 hours ahead by default, at most 8 days). A meeting id is its races' id without the race number, such as `thoroughbred_2026-11-17_AUS_scone`. Free: costs no credits.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Comma-separated racing codes: `thoroughbred`, `harness`, `greyhound`.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Comma-separated meeting countries: `AUS`, `NZL`.

parameters.name: starts_after
parameters.description: UTC date and time. Defaults to 6 hours ago.

parameters.name: starts_before
parameters.description: UTC date and time. At most 8 days after starts_after.

get.description: Resulted races in start order, each with its placings (runner number, position, name, and the TAB fixed and tote prices the placegetters paid), scratchings with their deductions, tote pool totals and tote dividends (win, place, quinella, exacta, trifecta, first four and the multi-race pools TAB declared). With no window the list covers the last 24 hours; a window may span at most 8 days. Results exist from 1 August 2026; dividends and prices paid come with them where the TAB result page was recorded. Costs 2 credits a call.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Comma-separated racing codes: `thoroughbred`, `harness`, `greyhound`.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Comma-separated meeting countries: `AUS`, `NZL`.

parameters.name: starts_after
parameters.description: UTC date and time. Defaults to 24 hours ago.

parameters.name: starts_before
parameters.description: UTC date and time. Defaults to now. At most 8 days after starts_after.

get.description: The full result of one race: placings with the prices paid (TAB fixed win and place, tote win and place, and Betfair Starting Price), scratchings with deductions, tote pools and dividends, and `betfair_sp`: the Betfair Starting Price of every runner for win and place with the pre-play and in-play traded range and volume (AUD), from Betfair's published BSP files (Australian races; they arrive the day after the race). `result` is null until the race is resulted. Positions are the placegetters' (first four). Costs 1 credit a call.

TAB tote pools for one race: the total in each pool (AUD), each runner's tote win and place dividend, and, once the race is resulted, the declared dividends by pool. `stage` is `approximate` while betting is open (the dividends move with the pool until it closes) and `final` after the result; null when the pools have not been read yet. Read about every 20 minutes in the three hours before a race and every minute in the last 15. Costs 1 credit a call.

Pro and Business only. Market movers across races still to run: for each runner the opening win price (the first price any bookmaker showed, and who) against the median and the best current fixed-odds win price, largest move first. `change` is (median now - opening) / opening: negative is firming, positive is drifting. Only prices observed in the last 600 seconds count, Betfair Exchange is not part of the median, and a runner whose opening price came from a bookmaker outside your request is left out. Looks at races from now to `starts_before` (3 hours ahead by default, 24 at most). Answers are reused for 20 seconds. Costs 10 credits a call.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Comma-separated racing codes.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Comma-separated meeting countries: `AUS`, `NZL`.

parameters.name: starts_before
parameters.description: UTC date and time within the next 24 hours. Defaults to 3 hours ahead.

parameters.name: min_change
parameters.description: Smallest move to list, as a fraction of the opening price.

get.description: Pro and Business only. Racing arbs on the win market in races still to run: the best fixed-odds win price at a bookmaker against the Betfair Exchange win lay price, where backing at the bookmaker and laying on the exchange returns a profit whichever way the race goes. `margin` = back x (1 - commission) / (lay - commission) - 1, the profit per unit staked on the back bet; `lay_stake_per_unit` = back / (lay - commission). `commission` is the exchange commission you pay (0.05 unless you pass yours; `meta.commission` echoes it). Both prices were observed in the last 600 seconds; `lay.size` is the AUD available at the lay price, so check it covers your lay stake, and check both prices before betting. Place markets are not compared (place terms differ between a bookmaker and the exchange). Looks at races from now to `starts_before` (3 hours ahead by default, 24 at most). Answers are reused for 20 seconds. Costs 10 credits a call.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Comma-separated racing codes.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Comma-separated meeting countries: `AUS`, `NZL`.

parameters.name: starts_before
parameters.description: UTC date and time within the next 24 hours. Defaults to 3 hours ahead.

parameters.name: commission
parameters.description: Exchange commission as a fraction.

get.description: Form for every runner of a race: `form_figures` (the last-starts figures shown on the TAB race page, newest last) and `starts`, the runner's last starts before this race that SockOdds recorded, newest first: date, meeting, distance, class, track condition, jockey, trainer, barrier, weight, finishing position, field size and the prices it started at (TAB fixed, tote, Betfair SP). Recorded starts begin on 1 August 2026 (`meta.recorded_from`), so a runner's earlier career is not listed. `position` is 1 to 4 for a placegetter and null for a runner that finished further back. Runners are matched by name within a racing code. Costs 1 credit a call.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Starts per runner.

get.description: One runner's recorded starts, newest first, by racing code and name (case, punctuation and a country suffix such as (NZ) are ignored). The same fields as a race's form. Recorded starts begin on 1 August 2026. Costs 1 credit a call.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The runner's name.

get.description: Strike rates for each runner's jockey (the driver in harness), trainer and the jockey and trainer together, over the `days` before the race: starts, wins, seconds, thirds, `win_rate` (wins / starts) and `place_rate` (first three / starts). Counted only from races SockOdds recorded (from 1 August 2026) in the same racing code, so they are rates over that record, not career figures. Greyhounds have a trainer only. Costs 1 credit a call.

Strike rates for one jockey (or driver), one trainer, or the two together, by name within a racing code, over the last `days` days of recorded races: starts, wins, seconds, thirds, win and place rate, and the first and last recorded start. Give `jockey`, `trainer` or both. Costs 1 credit a call.

parameters.name: jockey
parameters.description: Jockey or driver name.

get.description: Pro and above. Arbitrage: two prices at two different bookmakers that cover both sides of one market, so backing both in the listed proportions returns a profit whichever side wins. Upcoming events only, best profit first, 25 a page by default, up to 100. The list is recomputed about every four minutes from the prices SockOdds records; each entry carries the time each price was observed, when the entry was computed and when it expires. By default an entry is listed only while both prices were observed in the last 600 seconds (`max_age`). Only bookmakers your key may read are used. Costs 10 credits a call; an empty answer costs nothing. Prices move: check the price at the bookmaker before acting on any entry.

parameters.name: min_edge
parameters.description: Lowest profit to list, in percent of the total stake.

get.description: Pro and above. Low holds: the best price on each side of one market at two different bookmakers, where the two together carry almost no margin. `hold_pct` is that combined margin in percent (0 is break-even). Lowest hold first. Filters, paging, freshness and metering are as for arbitrage; `bookmakers` keeps the entries whose two prices are both at the named bookmakers.

parameters.name: max_hold
parameters.description: Highest combined margin to list, in percent.

get.description: Pro and above. Middles: two bets on different lines of one market at two bookmakers (over 44.5 at one, under 47.5 at the other), so both win when the result lands in the gap. `gap` is the distance between the lines, `middle_profit_pct` the profit in percent of the total stake when both win, and `profit_pct` the result when only one wins (negative unless the pair is also an arbitrage). Largest middle profit first. `min_edge` is the lowest `middle_profit_pct` to list. Filters, paging, freshness and metering are as for arbitrage.

parameters.name: min_edge
parameters.description: Lowest middle profit to list, in percent of the total stake.

get.description: Pro and above. Positive expected value: a bookmaker price longer than the fair price of the outcome. `fair` says how the fair price was made: `sharp_book` (one sharp bookmaker's two-sided market with its margin removed, named in `fair.bookmaker`), `exchange` (an exchange's back and lay prices) or `consensus` (the margin-free prices of `fair.books` other bookmakers, combined; never the bookmaker being priced). `ev_pct` is the expected profit in percent of the stake and `kelly_pct` the full-Kelly stake in percent of bankroll. Highest `ev_pct` first. Upcoming events only; freshness, paging and metering are as for arbitrage. An estimate, not a guarantee: a fair price is a model of the market, and prices move.

parameters.name: min_edge
parameters.description: Lowest expected value to list, in percent.

parameters.name: fair
parameters.description: Comma-separated fair-price methods to keep: `sharp_book`, `exchange`, `consensus`.

get.description: Pro and above. Fair prices for a league's events: each market's prices with the bookmaker margin removed. The base is Pinnacle's own two-sided (or three-way) market when Pinnacle prices every outcome of it (`fair.source` `sharp_book`); otherwise the median of every bookmaker that prices the whole market, each with its own margin removed, when at least three do (`consensus`). A market with neither base is left out, as are markets whose runners are players or scores. Each outcome carries its fair probability and fair decimal odds, and `best_price`: the best current price among the bookmakers your key may read, with its edge against the fair price. With no start window the list holds events that started at most 12 hours ago and upcoming ones, in start order, 25 a page at most. Main lines only unless `alternates=true`. Costs 5 credits a call; an empty answer costs nothing.
Pro and above. Fair prices for one event, as `/fair-odds` describes them. `bookmakers` limits both the bookmakers a consensus is built from and the bookmakers `best_price` is chosen among.

Pro and above. The closing line of one event: each bookmaker's opening and closing price per outcome (as `snapshots=opening,closing` returns them), the fair closing price per outcome (`closing_fair`, built from the closing prices as `/fair-odds` builds a fair price) and `opening_clv_pct`, the closing line value of each bookmaker's opening price: how far that price beat the fair closing price, in percent (positive beat the close). Give `outcome_id` and `odds` together to get the closing line value of your own bet in `bet`. Without `markets` the main markets are read (winner, result, handicap and the game totals); name up to 20 market keys for others. Closing prices are null until the event has started. Costs 10 credits a call.

parameters.name: outcome_id
parameters.description: The outcome you bet on. Give it with `odds`.

parameters.name: odds
parameters.description: The decimal odds you took. Give it with `outcome_id`.

get.description: Pro and above. Line moves in one league: markets whose main line (handicap, totals, player and team over/unders) changed at one or more bookmakers in the last `window` minutes, upcoming events only. Each bookmaker counts once, by its net move in the window (a line that moved and came back is not a move). `steam` is true when at least `min_books` bookmakers moved the same way and they are at least two thirds of the bookmakers that moved; `sharp` is true when Pinnacle is among them. `from_line` and `to_line` are the median line of those bookmakers before and after; for a handicap the line is the home side's (competitor 1 in tennis). Steam first, then the most bookmakers. Lines are sampled every few minutes, so a move is timed to the sample that first saw it. Markets with no line (head to head) are not covered. Costs 10 credits a call; an empty answer costs nothing.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: Minutes to look back, in steps of 5.

parameters.name: min_books
parameters.description: Fewest bookmakers that moved the same way.

parameters.name: steam
parameters.description: true lists only steam moves.

EventsStartsAfter.name: starts_after
EventsStartsAfter.description: UTC date and time. With neither starts_after nor starts_before, the list starts 48 hours ago (live and upcoming games plus the last two days), and international cricket Tests (league cricket) are listed for six days from their start; name a window to list older games.

EventsStartsBefore.name: starts_before
EventsStartsBefore.description: UTC date and time. Give starts_after, starts_before or both to list games outside the default window (from 48 hours ago; six days for cricket Tests).

GroupBy.name: group_by
GroupBy.description: How prices are grouped. `market` (the default) lists each market and outcome once, with every bookmaker's price under the outcome in `prices`, best price first. `bookmaker` lists each bookmaker with its own copy of the markets, the shape v1 launched with.

NonParticipantFilter.name: non_participant
NonParticipantFilter.description: Comma-separated non-participation rules (`void`, `loses`, `under`, `fair_price`). Keeps only player-market prices whose bookmaker settles a player who takes no part by one of these rules; prices on every other market are unaffected. For example `non_participant=void` keeps only player prices that are refunded when the player does not play.

MaxAge.name: max_age
MaxAge.description: Oldest price to use, in seconds since it was observed. An entry is listed only while every price in it is at most this old.

Devig.name: devig
Devig.description: How the margin is removed. `proportional` (the default) divides each implied probability by their sum. `power` raises each to the one exponent that makes them sum to 1, which takes more margin off long prices.

participants.description: Who contests an event. Team sports use the participant roles home and away; individual sports (tennis, mixed martial arts) use competitor_1 and competitor_2.

ungraded_periods.description: Periods this market is quoted for but not yet graded, because no results source supplies the statistic yet. Results for quotes in these periods stay pending. Listed where audited; its absence is not a guarantee that a period grades. It is per market across all its sports, so a period is listed if it is ungraded in any of them.

non_participant.description: Player markets only. The non-participation rules a price on this market may carry (see the `non_participant` of each price in the odds routes). Every player-market price carries one.

sides.description: Side keys, or participants when each outcome is a player runner, or scores for exact-score outcomes. A market offers home and away only in team sports and competitor_1 and competitor_2 only in tennis and UFC.

role.description: home and away in team sports. In tennis and UFC, competitor_1 and competitor_2 in the order the event's trusted fixture source lists them; there is no home side.

cricket_format.description: Official format, present for supported cricket events

ExchangeContract.description: Native buy contract underlying the enclosing rounded decimal odds. Available is a native quantity; price is the fraction of payout per share/contract. Buy cost equals price times available times payout_per_contract before fees; omitted payout means 1. Novig pays USD 0.01 per contract, Fanatics Markets USD 1. An opposite contract is not a lay.

payout_per_contract.description: Native monetary payout in liquidity.currency per contract; omitted means 1 for existing feeds.

ExchangeLiquidity.description: Verified native exchange depth for this outcome, line and quoted back price, at the enclosing price's observed_at. Available amounts are resting stake, not guaranteed account limits or lay liability. Absent when not reported or the current price is unavailable.

market_ref.description: Native exchange market reference; joins the market-level exchanges entry.

offer_ref.description: BetOpenly offer identifier when the feed supplies no native market ID.

currency.description: Capture currency when verified; null means unknown. Never infer currency from bookmaker region.

available_to_back.description: Unrounded amount available at the enclosing decimal_odds.

decimal_odds.description: Best lay price for this same selection and line.

available.description: Resting stake available at this lay price, not liability.

ExchangeMarket.description: One native exchange market's reported activity. Missing matched_volume means unreported, never zero. Kalshi and Novig traded_contracts is a count, not money. Never sum runner volumes. A native market can span canonical lines; the same market_ref total may therefore appear under multiple lines and must not be added together. Current observations only; no liquidity history or opening/closing volume is promised.

matched_volume.description: Verified monetary volume from the native market, never a contract count or open-order activity.

traded_contracts.description: Kalshi volume_fp or Novig native market volume in contracts. This is not matched money.

side.description: A catalogue side key or player runner ID. Team sports name participants home and away; tennis and UFC name them competitor_1 and competitor_2, the event's participant roles. Exact-score outcomes use score_<home>_<away> in registry home/away order with integer scores from 0 through 999. Half-time/full-time outcomes use <half-time>_<full-time> with each stage home, draw or away (home_draw means home leads at half time and it is a draw at full time).

line.description: The outcome's own line. On a handicap each outcome carries its own figure: home -6.5 with away +6.5, and in tennis competitor_1 -2.5 with competitor_2 +2.5 (games). Null when the market has no line.

available.description: Whether the current quote is available and fresh. Stale or withdrawn quotes appear only when snapshots are requested and carry null current prices.

non_participant.description: Player markets only, and only when the rule is not `void`: this shape stays byte for byte the launch body, so an absent value on a player market means `void`. Grouped by market, every player price carries it.

opening.description: The first quote before the `snapshots` cutoff, skipping withdrawals. Null when there is none.

closing.description: The last quote before the `snapshots` cutoff. Null when there is none. For every sport but MMA it is also null when that last row is a withdrawal (the book pulled the price before `scheduled_start`); it never falls back to an earlier price. For an MMA bout withdrawals are skipped, so closing is the last price offered before the cutoff.

NonParticipant.description: Player markets only: how this bookmaker settles this price when the player takes no part, from the bookmaker's own published rules. `void`: the stake is returned. `loses`: all-in, the bet stands and loses. `under`: the bet settles as the Under (or No) side. `fair_price`: the venue settles at a fair price it sets. /v1/results grades the outcomes of a player who took no part `void`; a price whose rule is not `void` settles differently at that bookmaker.

Price.description: One bookmaker's current price for an outcome.

available.description: Whether the quote is available and fresh. Stale or withdrawn quotes appear only when snapshots are requested and carry null current prices.

opening.description: The first quote before the `snapshots` cutoff, skipping withdrawals. Null when there is none.

closing.description: The last quote before the `snapshots` cutoff. Null when there is none. For every sport but MMA it is also null when that last row is a withdrawal (the book pulled the price before `scheduled_start`); it never falls back to an earlier price. For an MMA bout withdrawals are skipped, so closing is the last price offered before the cutoff.

side.description: A catalogue side key or player runner ID, as on Outcome.

line.description: The outcome's own line: home -6.5 with away +6.5. Null when the market has no line.

prices.description: Every bookmaker price for this outcome, best first: highest decimal odds, then bookmaker key. prices[0] is the best price among the bookmakers asked for. A price with no current odds (snapshots only) comes last.

alternate.description: True when this line is not the market's main line. Alternate lines appear only with alternates=true.

outcomes.description: In the market's side order (home, draw, away; over, under); players and scores by name.

OddsEvent.description: An event with its prices grouped by market (the default). Markets come in catalogue order, then period, subject and line.

OddsEventByBookmaker.description: An event with its prices grouped by bookmaker (group_by=bookmaker), the shape v1 launched with.

BoxScore.description: The box score of a finished event: the official statistics results are graded from (the score by period, event and team totals, and the player statistics SockOdds grades, for players the registry identifies), as the source publishes them. Corrections at the source increase `revision`. Players are identified by player ID, with the name and team the player registry holds now; a player merged since is shown under the ID he was merged into.

revision.description: Increases each time the official box score changes (a correction at the source).

observed_at.description: When the official source was read for this revision.

periods.description: One entry per period the source scores (period keys as in /v1/leagues).

void.description: Present and true when the period was voided.

home.description: Home team score in the period.

away.description: Away team score in the period.

totals.description: Event totals in the period, by statistic (for example points, goals, corners).

home_stats.description: Home team statistics in the period.

away_stats.description: Away team statistics in the period.

competitors.description: Tennis and UFC: the official winner (competitor_1 or competitor_2), how the contest ended, and for UFC the method.

competitor_games.description: Tennis: games won by each competitor.

cricket.description: Cricket: the official result (format and outcome).

team.description: The team the player registry holds for the player now.

stats.description: Statistics by period, then by statistic: { "full": { "points": 31, "rebounds": 9 } }.

did_not_play.description: By period: statistics the official source voids because the player took no part.

unmatched.description: Athletes the official source lists that no published registry player is identified with (including an identity under review): the source's own athlete ID and name. null when the read did not list the source's athletes.

withheld_players.description: Players in the box score whose identity the registry does not publish now (under review or merged); they are not listed.

box_score.description: Always present on /v1/results: the official statistics the result is graded from, or null while none have been read.

settlement.description: complete when every quoted market on the event is settled; partial while any market is still pending.

pending_markets.description: How many quoted markets on the event are still pending. A market is pending until official evidence settles every one of its outcomes.

verdict.description: half_won / half_lost: an Asian quarter line (x.25 / x.75) whose two half stakes split: one half won (or lost) at the quoted price and the other half refunded.

dead_heat_factor.description: Dead heats only: the share of the stake paid at the quoted price. The rest of the stake is lost.

state.description: Australian state or territory; null in New Zealand.

jumped_at.description: When the race was first seen off.

class_conditions.description: Class and conditions as TAB states them, such as `3YO+ MDN`. Null until the TAB race page has been read.

track_condition.description: Track rating as stated, such as `GOOD4` or `SOFT6`.

form_figures.description: Last-starts figures as shown on the TAB race page, newest last (`x` is a spell).

win.description: Fixed-odds win price (decimal); on Betfair Exchange the best back price.

place.description: Fixed-odds place price (decimal); on Betfair Exchange the best back price.

win_back_size.description: Betfair Exchange only. AUD available at the back price.

win_lay_size.description: Betfair Exchange only. AUD available at the lay price.

win_matched.description: Betfair Exchange only. AUD matched on the runner.

place_winners.description: Betfair Exchange only. How many places the place market pays.

exchange_back.description: Closing only. Betfair Exchange back price at the jump.

exchange_lay.description: Closing only. Betfair Exchange lay price at the jump.

OpportunityLeg.description: One of the two bets of a pair.

side.description: A catalogue side key (over, under, home, away, yes, no ...).

line.description: The outcome's own line. Null when the market has no line.

stake_pct.description: Share of the total stake to place on this leg, in percent, so both results return the same. Null on a middle.

observed_at.description: When this price was observed at the bookmaker.

id.description: Stable while the two prices do not change.

implied_sum.description: The two implied probabilities added. Below 1 is an arbitrage.

profit_pct.description: Arbitrage and middles: profit in percent of the total stake when one leg wins. Negative on a middle that is not also an arbitrage.

hold_pct.description: Low holds: the combined margin of the two prices, in percent.

gap.description: Middles: the distance between the two lines.

middle_profit_pct.description: Middles: profit in percent of the total stake when both legs win.

price_age_seconds.description: Age of the older of the two prices when the response was built.

expires_at.description: The entry is dropped at this time unless a later pass finds it again.

bookmaker.description: The bookmaker or exchange the fair price comes from. Null for a consensus.

devig.description: Consensus only: how each bookmaker's margin was removed.

books.description: How many bookmakers the fair price was built from.

ev_pct.description: Expected profit in percent of the stake.

kelly_pct.description: Full-Kelly stake in percent of bankroll.

bookmaker.description: The sharp bookmaker. Null for a consensus.

overround.description: The implied probabilities of the base added: the sharp bookmaker's own, or the median across the consensus bookmakers. 1.03 is a 3 percent margin.

ev_pct.description: Edge of this price against the fair price, in percent. Negative when the best price is shorter than fair.

closing_fair.description: How the fair closing price was built. Null when no bookmaker closed the whole market (or before the event starts).

opening_clv_pct.description: Closing line value of this bookmaker's opening price against the fair closing price, in percent. Positive beat the close.

bet.description: Present when outcome_id and odds are given.

clv_pct.description: Your odds against the fair closing price, in percent. Null until there is a fair closing price.

direction.description: Which way most bookmakers moved the line.

sharp.description: True when Pinnacle is among the bookmakers that moved with the majority.

from_line.description: Median line of the majority before their move.

to_line.description: Median line of the majority after it.

observed_at.description: When the bookmaker's latest line in the window was first seen.

OddsEvents.description: Current prices, grouped by market unless group_by=bookmaker

OddsEvent.description: Event prices, grouped by market unless group_by=bookmaker

RacingData.description: Racing data in the usual `{data, meta, links}` envelope. The fields are described on the operation and shown, with invented sample values, in the racing guide.

ClosingEvent.description: Opening and closing prices with closing line value
